div.head: VI Atr Lat 36
div.ab: K. Si etiam quisquam de excommunicatis, nisi causa refugii, in regis presumpserit presentia ante penitentię satisfactionem peractam consistere, facultatum proscriptione dampnetur.
div.note: Latin paraphrase of VI Atr (early 11th c.; K = Cotton Claudius A III f. 30, perhaps by Archbishop Wulfstan), text in column K (Liebermann’s text; until October 2026 in column T). Liebermann gives no German translation for it: for the meaning see the matching Old English chapter of VI Atr above, which it paraphrases (Liebermann prints in small type the words that correspond exactly to the Old English).; T: corrected against Gesetze I, October 2026 (was “(Liebermann’s Latin Paraphrase)”, now “∅ (moved to K)”)

note.seg: Hier stimmt die Paraphrase L gegen K zu amansumad in V 29; dieses Wort mag also fürs Gesetz von 1008 als authentisch gelten. Vielleicht bewusst greift K zurück auf I Em 3 = II 4 blod geate.—Meineid (s. d. Gl 6. 10) steht neben Mord auch sonst, u. a. in den Quellen dieses Stücks (EGu 11 = o. 7 und V Atr 24f. = o. 28, 2f.) und hat Kirchenbann zur Folge; s. Gl Exkommunikation 11k

Here the paraphrase L agrees, against K, with amansumad in V 29; this word may therefore be regarded as authentic for the law of 1008. K, perhaps deliberately, goes back to I Em 3 = II 4 blod geate. — Perjury (see that word in Gl 6. 10) appears alongside murder elsewhere too, among others in the sources of this piece (EGu 11 = above 7 and V Atr 24f. = above 28, 2f.), and entails excommunication; see Gl Exkommunikation 11k
‘towards the kindred’ (of the slain man) II Em 4
Wie o. 35¹ bleibt Todesstrafe, die V 29 droht, fort
As above 35¹, the death penalty threatened by V 29 is omitted
